housing: Bromsgrove is a mostly owner-occupied district between Birmingham and Worcestershire's countryside, much of it Green Belt. Bromsgrove town has Victorian terraces near the centre and post-war and modern estates around it. The northern villages such as Rubery, Hagley and Wythall are commuter areas with family houses for Birmingham. Private lets are mainly terraced and semi-detached houses and some flats in the town.
checkinTips: Victorian terraces near Bromsgrove town centre and Aston Fields: photograph rear yards, outside drains and any damp in rear kitchens.
Larger detached houses in Barnt Green and Hagley: photograph driveways, gates, garages and gardens as well as the rooms.
Canalside homes in Alvechurch: photograph garden boundaries and any damp near ground level.
Post-war semis in Rubery and Catshill: photograph any extensions, conservatories and their roofs for leaks.
Gardens next to Green Belt fields: photograph fences, hedges and gates, which often need repair after winter.
tenantHelp: Tenants can report disrepair, damp or unsafe homes to the council's private sector housing team, which can inspect and require landlords to put things right.
